Generujemy próbkę z określonych odcinków.

  • decydujemy jaki ma być rozmiar tej próbki (ponieważ musimy określić rozmiar statystyki)

def rvs_order_brutal(n: int, m: int):
    # create probe size (m x 1 with n values)
    probe = np.array([np.sort(s_dist.rvs((int(n)))) for _ in range(m)])
    return probe

Exercise 2 (presentation) (Records)¶

Let $X_0, \ldots, X_n, \ldots \sim_{\mathrm{i.i.d.}} F$. Where $F$ is continous one dimensional probability distribution.

We want to calculate $R_n$ where $R_n$ is defined as follows:

$$\begin{align*}T_0 & := 0, R_0 = X_0 \\ T_{j+1} &:= \min\{i: X_i>R_j\}, R_{j+1}=X_{T_{j+1}} \end{align*}$$

Theoretical results¶

cdf¶

We want to find conditional cdf (It depends only on recent value), we write that as: $$\begin{align*} F_{R_{i}|R_{i-1}}(y|x) & =cdf_{R_i|R_{i-1}}(y|x) = \mathbb{P}[R_{i} \leq y|R_{i-1}=x] = \mathbb{P}[X\leq y|X>x]= \frac{\mathbb{P}[X\leq y, X>x]}{1-\mathbb{P}[X\leq x]}=  \\  & = \frac{{\mathrm{cdf}_{X}(y) - \mathrm{cdf}_{X}(x)}}{1-\mathrm{cdf}_{X}(x)} \end{align*}$$

pdf¶

To obtain pdf de differentiate function due to $y$: $$\begin{align*} f_{R_{i}|R_{i-1}}(y|x) &=\mathrm{pdf}_{R_{i}|R_{i-1}}(y|x) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}y}\mathrm{cdf_{R_{i}|R_{i-1}}(y|x)} = \\ &= \frac{{\mathrm{pdf}_{X}(y)}}{1-\mathrm{cdf}_{X}(x)}, & y & >x \end{align*}$$

marginal distributions¶

To obtain marginal distribution we obtain from definition $$f_{R_{i}}(y)=\int_{-\infty}^{y}f_{R_{i}|R_{i-1}}(y|x)\underbrace {f_{R_{i-1}}(x)}_{\text{recurrence}}\mathrm{d}x$$ But here we obtain recurennce relation.

Recurrence¶

Marginal for $R_1$": $$\begin{align} f_{R_{1}}(y) & =\int_{-\infty}^{y}f_{R_{1}|R_{0}}(y|x){f_{R_{0}}(x)}\mathrm{d}x = \int_{-\infty}^{y} \frac{{f_{X}(y)}}{1-F_{X}(x)}f_{R_{0}=X}(x)\mathrm{d}x= \\ & = \left[\begin{cases} u=F_{X}(x) \\ \mathrm{d}u=f_{X}(x)\mathrm{d}x \end{cases}\right] = f_{X}(y)\int_{0}^{F_{X}(y)} \frac{1}{1-u}\mathrm{d}u = f_{X}(y)[-\ln(1-u)|_{0}^{F_{X}(y)}] = \\ & = f_{X}(y)(-\ln(1-F_{X}(y))) \end{align}$$ Marginal for $R_2$" $$\begin{align} f_{R_{2}}(y) & =\int_{-\infty}^{y}f_{R_{2}|R_{1}}(y|x){f_{R_{1}}(x)}\mathrm{d}x = \int_{-\infty}^{y} \frac{{f_{X}(y)}}{1-F_{X}(x)}f_{R_{1}}(x)\mathrm{d}x= \\ & =\int_{-\infty}^{y} \frac{{f_{X}(y)}}{1- F_{X}(x)}\cdot f_{X}(x)(-\ln(1-F(x)))\mathrm{d}x = \\ & = \begin{bmatrix} u=F_{X}(x) \\ \mathrm{d}u=f_{X}(x)\mathrm{d}x \end{bmatrix} = f_{X}(y)\int_{0}^{F_{X}(y)} \frac{-(\ln(1-u))}{1-u}\mathrm{d}u = \\ & = \begin{bmatrix} w=-\ln(1-u) \\ \mathrm{d}w= \frac{{-1}}{1-u}\mathrm{d}u \end{bmatrix} = f_{X}(y)\int_{0}^{-\ln(1-F_{X}(y))} f_{X}(y)w\mathrm{d}w=f_{X}(y)\frac{w^{2}}{2}|_{0}^{-\ln(1-F_{X}(y))} = \\ & =\frac{f_{X}(y)}{2} [-\ln(1-F_{X}(y))]^{2} \end{align}$$ Marginal for $R_n$ $$\begin{align} f_{R_{n}}(y) & =\int_{-\infty}^{y}f_{R_{2}|R_{1}}(y|x){f_{R_{1}}(x)}\mathrm{d}x = \int_{-\infty}^{y} \frac{{f_{X}(y)}}{1-F_{X}(x)}f_{R_{1}}(x)\mathrm{d}x= \\ & =\int_{-\infty}^{y} \frac{{f_{X}(y)}}{1- F_{X}(x)}\cdot \frac{1}{(n-1)!} f_{X}(x)(-\ln(1-F(x)))^{n-1}\mathrm{d}x = \\ & = \begin{bmatrix} u=F_{X}(x) \\ \mathrm{d}u=f_{X}(x)\mathrm{d}x \end{bmatrix} = \frac{f_{X}(y)}{(n-1)!}\int_{0}^{F_{X}(y)} \frac{-(\ln(1-u))^{n-1}}{1-u}\mathrm{d}u = \\ & = \begin{bmatrix} w=-\ln(1-u) \\ \mathrm{d}w= \frac{{-1}}{1-u}\mathrm{d}u \end{bmatrix} = \frac{f_{X}(y)}{(n-1)!}\int_{0}^{-\ln(1-F_{X}(y))} f_{X}(y)w^{n-1}\mathrm{d}w= \frac{f_{X}(y)}{(n-1)!} \frac{w^{n}}{n}|_{0}^{-\ln(1-F_{X}(y))} = \\ & =\frac{f_{X}(y)}{n!} [-\ln(1-F_{X}(y))]^{n} \end{align}$$

Simulation solution¶

To simulate process efficiently we use inverse sampling to always obtain suitable sample:

  1. We generate $\mathrm{probe} \sim F$ at random
  2. We take $l_i = \mathrm{cdf}_F(\mathrm{probe}_{i-1})$
  3. We take $X_i \sim \mathrm{Unif}([l, 1])$
  4. We take $R_i = F^{-1}(X)$
  5. repeat 2-4

# #TODO 
def rvs_record_single(k: int, dist: stats.rv_continuous | stats.rv_discrete):
    '''
    In this solution i use different approach when i will be able to accept all probes using inverse sampling method:
    - Generate first probe
    - Take it through distribution and divide domain X ~ U(dist.cdf(probe(i)), 1)
    - we than take dist.ppf(X) (inverse of cdf) 
    '''
    # params 
    ## here we take n+1 probes we omit first one 
    records = np.zeros(k+1)
    curr_max = 0 
    curr_size = 0
    ## first record
    records[0] = dist.rvs()
    
    # obtaining other index
    for i in range(1, k+1):
        # cdf (probe[i-1])
        left_margin = dist.cdf(records[i-1])
        # X ~ Unif(cdf, 1)
        sample = stats.uniform(left_margin, 1-left_margin).rvs()
        # cdf^-1 (X)
        records[i] = dist.ppf(sample) 
           
    return records

    ## helper function

def rvs_record(n: int, k: int, dist: stats.rv_continuous | stats.rv_discrete):
    '''
    Wrapper for taking n samples from this distribution
    '''
    # generate multiple probes    
    probes = np.array([rvs_record_single(k, dist) for _ in range(n)])
    # reshape it into (n x k) array
    return probes

def plot_theoretical(k: int, domain: list[int],dist: stats.rv_discrete | stats.rv_continuous):
    # unpack border
    l, r = domain
    X_dom = np.linspace(l, r, 100 * (r-l))

    # TODO - był błąd 
    numerator  = dist.pdf(X_dom) * (- np.log(1-dist.cdf(X_dom)))**k
    denominator = math.factorial(k)
    return X_dom, numerator/denominator

    plt.title(f'Pdf and histograms of {key}')

Exercise 3 - ćw 1.17 p. 44¶

Measure of location

Let $X_1, ..., X_n$ be i.i.d. sample from $F$-symetric distribution that is such ous $c=\mathbb{E} X = \mathrm{med}X$.

Lets calculate estimators:

  • $\hat{c} = \bar{X}$
  • $\hat{c} = \mathrm{median}(X)$
  • $\hat{c} = \frac{\min(X) - \max(X)}{2}$

Make graphs (histograms) in same scale (we tract those estimator as random variables - so we have their distribution)d

Question - which estimator converges the fastest !!! (smallest variance)
